text: Damian is coeliac, properly strict about it, not just avoiding bread. Worth remembering before the team lunch on May 14.
Owen lives in Leeds now, in a flat above a bike shop near the station. His sister Ana is still in Bristol.
Remind me to ask Carmen how her driving test went on Tuesday morning. She was really nervous about the roundabouts.
Shira only drinks oat milk flat whites and absolutely hates anything with coconut in it.
Jonah supports Everton and has had a season ticket since he was nine. He goes with his dad to every home game.
Caitlin's dinner party on June 3rd has been called off because her landlord is doing work on the kitchen.

Kate mentioned she's started knitting again after about five years off. She's making a blanket for her niece, chunky cream wool with a cable pattern, and wants to try Fair Isle colourwork next. She swears by the yarn from that little shop on Albert Road and hates the acrylic stuff from the big craft chains. A nice skein from there would go down really well for her birthday.
Need to pick up the dry cleaning before Friday at 3pm and book the car in for its MOT.
Talked to Ximena after book club. She's halfway through the Wolf Hall trilogy and loves anything set in the Tudor period. Her husband Tunde can't stand historical fiction, which she finds hilarious.
Lola works at the council in planning, has done for about six years. Her partner Rana is a paramedic.
Thabo is vegan as of this year. Don't forget to tell the restaurant when I book for Saturday at 7.
Salma's mum has her hip operation on 9/22. Salma is going to stay with her for a week afterwards.
Fiona and her husband are celebrating their tenth anniversary on July 18. They're going back to Lisbon, where they got engaged.
Yaw plays five-a-side on Wednesdays and is obsessed with Arsenal. He's also really into vinyl, mainly seventies Afrobeat and highlife.
I'm taking Petra to the airport tomorrow morning at 6. Her flight to Toronto is at 9:40.
Jamal is allergic to tree nuts, including almonds. He carries an EpiPen. Must check the cake ingredients before his son's party on the 12th.

Hiroshi lives in Kyoto at the moment, in a tiny old townhouse near the river, but he's moving to Osaka on March 15th because his company is merging two offices. He's not thrilled about it. His girlfriend Rana is staying in Kyoto for now, so they'll be doing weekends. He says his cat Mochi already hates the carrier, so the train journey should be fun.
Magda's daughter graduates on May 20th at 2pm. Remind me to send Magda a card that week.
Spoke to Tendai on the phone. Her brother Lwazi just got into the national rugby sevens squad. She's thrilled and a bit worried about his knee.
Lior said he's been struggling since the redundancy. He's applying everywhere but hasn't heard back. I should check in with him next Monday.

Mehmet's favourite thing is proper Turkish tea, strong, in the little tulip glasses, with two sugar cubes. He thinks English breakfast tea is basically dishwater. He also loves pistachio baklava but only from the bakery in Green Lanes, and he doesn't eat pork. His wife Magda is the opposite and drinks about six cans of Diet Coke a day.

Emily works as a nurse at St James's, on the children's ward, mostly nights. She lives in Headingley with two flatmates and her boyfriend lives in Harrogate. Her parents are in Cornwall and her older sister Fiona is a teacher in Exeter with three kids of her own. She says she's the only one in the family who left the south west.
Adaeze is doing Dry January again, and she's going pescatarian from the start of the year as well. Coffee is the one thing she won't give up.
Michael has a dog called Biscuit, a very nervous rescue greyhound. Biscuit is having a tooth out on Thursday afternoon.
Graham collects old railway posters and has about forty framed in his hallway. He'd love one of the Scarborough ones if I ever see one at a fair.
Note to self: Joseph's birthday is October 30. He's been dropping hints about a new pair of running headphones.
Ava and Jonah are expecting their first baby in February. They haven't picked names but Ava wants something short.
Carmen lives in Valencia with her parents and her younger brother. Her grandmother lives in the flat downstairs.
Ask Owen how the interview at the architecture firm went. It was on 10/14 at 11am and he said it felt rushed.
Kate can't eat dairy, but she's fine with goat's cheese. Odd, but good to know.

Shira plays the cello in a community orchestra. They have a concert on November 8th at 7:30 at St Mary's, and she's playing a short solo. She said she hasn't slept properly in a week thinking about it. I'd like to go if I'm free, and I should text her good luck that afternoon.
Finally sorted my own plans for half term. I'm driving up to my aunt's on the 24th and coming back the following Sunday evening.
Damian's wife Petra is pregnant again, due around April 2nd. Their eldest, Leo, is apparently thrilled about being a big brother.

Caitlin is a massive board game person. Wingspan, Terraforming Mars, Spirit Island, anything with lots of little wooden pieces and a rulebook the size of a phone book. She runs a games night every other Thursday at her flat and keeps a spreadsheet of who has won what. Her husband Thabo only plays Catan and gets furious when he loses. She's been eyeing the new Wingspan expansion.
Salma told me her son Yusuf starts secondary school on September 4th and is dreading the bus journey. Remind me to message her that evening to see how his first day went.
Tunde Brennan from accounts is retiring on December 15. There's leaving drinks the same day at 5pm at the Crown.
Thabo lives in Cape Town but works remotely for a Dutch company. His parents live in Durban.
Rana doesn't drink alcohol at all, so get some of the nice elderflower stuff for the barbecue on the 27th.

Called Fiona tonight. Her dad has been in hospital since last Wednesday with pneumonia, and she's exhausted from driving back and forth. They're hoping he'll be discharged by Friday morning. I need to ring her again on Sunday, and maybe drop off some food at hers this weekend so she doesn't have to cook.
Ximena's daughter Lola, who everyone calls Lolita, had her ballet exam on Saturday. Must remember to ask how it went.
Ana said she's started climbing at the bouldering wall near her office. She goes three times a week and is already on the blue routes.
Yaw's wedding in Accra was cancelled. They've decided to do a small registry office thing in London instead, sometime in the spring.
Hiroshi is a huge fan of Studio Ghibli and has a shelf of Totoro figures. He also plays the shamisen, which I didn't know.
Gym, then groceries. Need eggs, spinach, and something for Thursday's dinner.

Jamal's wife Adaeze is a GP at a practice in Salford, and they live in Eccles with their two boys, who are seven and ten. Jamal himself works in IT for the university. His brother is a pilot for some airline in Dubai, and his mum lives with them part of the year. Adaeze's family is mostly in Lagos.
Remind me to ask Emily if she wants to come to the gig on 11/2. She loves Fontaines D.C.
Mehmet Kaur's daughter has her first violin recital next Friday at 6pm. He's prouder than she is.
Tendai mentioned that Magda's husband passed away last month. The funeral was quiet. I should send Magda a note this week, nothing elaborate.

Michael and his partner Graham are moving to Brighton on June 30th, which I didn't expect at all. The removal van comes at 8am that morning. Michael has already found a job at a design studio there, starting Monday July 7, and Graham will keep working remotely. Remind me to text Michael on the 7th to see how the first day went.
Lwazi only eats halal meat and doesn't like spicy food at all, even mild curries are too much for him.
Petra is a structural engineer at a firm in Manchester. She grew up in Prague and her family still lives there.

Joseph is training for the Berlin marathon on September 27th. He's doing long runs every Sunday morning and says his left knee is starting to complain. Don't forget to ask how the eighteen-miler went this weekend, and send him a good luck message on the 26th.
Lunch with Lior went well. He's into fermenting things now: kimchi, sauerkraut, hot sauce. He promised me a jar of the hot sauce.
Kate's brother Jonah is getting married on August 9th in Galway. She's a bridesmaid and has the hen do on July 19.
Carmen and Owen have a new kitten called Pepper. Carmen sent me about thirty photos this morning.
Ava is learning Portuguese on Duolingo because her partner's family is from Porto. She has a 200-day streak and is weirdly competitive about it.
Note: Damian prefers red wine, mostly Rioja, and can't stand anything sweet. Good for Christmas.
Shira's grandad turns ninety on March 3rd. The family is hiring a hall for a lunch at 1pm, and she's in charge of the cake. She's asked if I can help her bake it the night before.
Rain all day. Nothing much happened, just tidied the spare room and watched the match.
Graham's son Owen has had a rough week at uni, homesick and behind on deadlines. Graham's driving down to see him tomorrow afternoon. I must remember to ask Graham on Friday how Owen's getting on.
